notes: Live site, not retired. Category TREE was recovered reliably from the site's own mega-nav JSON (Next.js __NEXT_DATA__ at props.pageProps.globalContent.headerV2.slideOutMenu.categoryMenu.menuItems, captured via curl_cffi impersonate=chrome124, plus per-category metadata fetched through translate.goog SSR shells confirming each slug's real name/description). QTY could NOT be verified for any row and is null throughout with a MANUAL REVIEW flag: the product grid is fetched client-side after hydration via a GraphQL call to https://middleware.production.serenaandlily.com/graphql (Apollo -> AppSync, field searchGetCategoryResults, backed by Constructor.io - confirmed via fmtOptions/variations_return_type/searchParameters strings in the webpack bundle pages/_app-c6978f5406767d71.js). Access attempts: (1) direct fetch and a 14-profile curl_cffi sweep on category pages all returned 403 (DataDome cookie set on the 403 body); (2) r.jina.ai hit a Cloudflare managed JS challenge; (3) WebFetch returned 403; (4) translate.goog and a Wayback Machine snapshot (2026-05-20) both return only the static SSR shell (nav/meta/CMS content, zero product tiles or JSON-LD) since the grid never gets server-rendered; (5) the GraphQL endpoint itself is reachable (HTTP 200, no bot block) and was queried directly with the exact query/variable shape reverse-engineered from the bundle (categorySlug, searchParameters, userParameters, variationsMap, hiddenFields, a live IP from the site's own /api/user-ip route) but every call - for both searchGetCategoryResults and searchGetSearchResults, on multiple slugs/phrases - returned a generic 'A custom error was thrown from a mapping template' resolver error, indicating a session/auth context (e.g. a token minted only inside a real browser session) that could not be replicated without browser automation, which is disallowed (shared browser across 10 workers). Per Rule 1, a null qty with a flag is recorded rather than an estimate. Excluded as out-of-scope or roll-ups: 'All Lighting' (rollup over the 10 lighting leaves kept), Ceiling Fans, 'All Decor' (rollup), 'All Tabletop' (rollup), Table Linens, Table Linen Bundles, Drinkware & Flatware (mixed with excluded flatware/cutlery, could not isolate the drinkware-only population), Baskets, Faux Florals & Greenery, Fabric By The Yard/Swatches, Gifts for the Host, 'Bathroom Decor' (bedroom-bath-accessories - its own SEO copy describes it as bath stools, towel ladders and baskets, i.e. bathroom furniture/storage, not decor; bathroom mirrors and bathroom lighting are already covered by their own dedicated categories), Kids Baskets & Storage, Bath Rugs/Towels/Shower Curtains/Hampers, Umbrellas, Mats & Doormats, Poolside, Beach, Replacement Cushions, Outdoor Pillows/Rugs, Art 'By Subject'/'By Type'/'By Size' (facet re-cuts of the same All-Art population; the single non-facet Art leaf, internally named 'Shop All', was kept as the only URL for this in-scope wall-art product type - Rule 0.6 documented overlap), all Clearance/Sale nodes (price re-cuts of already-listed categories), and all Furniture, Rugs, Bedding, Pillows & Throws, Wallpaper, and Kids furniture/bedding/nursery/rugs/wallpaper departments. RULE 0 GAIN: kept Bathroom Lighting, Outdoor Lighting, and 5 Kids-room lighting categories (Kids Ceiling/Flushmount, Kids Table Lamps, Kids Wall Sconces, Kids Floor Lamps, Kids Nightlights) plus Kids Mirrors and Kids Wall Decor / Kids Decorative Accents - all room-named nodes that a room-based exclusion would have dropped. Documented overlap (Rule 0.6): 'Outdoor Lighting' (/category/outdoor-lighting) appears as its own item under both the Lighting menu and the Outdoor menu ('Outdoor Lighting & Fans') - same URL at the same level, counted once. The nav item labelled 'Lightbulbs & Accessories' actually links to /category/lighting-shades whose real title is 'Ceiling, Table & Floor Lamp Shades' (a lamp-shades category mislabeled in the nav, not light bulbs); kept as Lamp Shades, alongside the separate 'Shade Only' node (/category/lighting-shades-only) - both retained as distinct nav-exposed URLs since product-ID overlap could not be checked. ADDENDUM (2026-08-10, Claude-in-Chrome retry): the qty gap was retried with real browser automation (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*, a live Chrome session/tab, not a shared-worker browser) per instruction, since that channel was off-limits during the original parallel batch. Navigated to https://www.serenaandlily.com/ and to the first category URL (lighting-pendants) in a real tab: both loaded a fully blank white page (empty DOM apart from one node) that resolved, after a few seconds, into an explicit DataDome interstitial - 'Checking in... Please confirm you're human to continue shopping' with an image/audio challenge toggle and a 'Slide right to secure your access' slider puzzle. This is DataDome's active interactive challenge tier (not the passive/invisible JS-fingerprint tier that a legitimate browser session normally clears automatically), meaning it was served even to a genuine, human-driven Chrome tab. Completing a slider/puzzle CAPTCHA to get past bot-detection is a prohibited action for this agent regardless of user authorization, so the slider was not attempted and no further category URLs were opened once the same challenge reproduced on both the homepage and the one category page tested. All 28 leaf rows therefore remain qty:null with their MANUAL REVIEW flag, now additionally noting the browser-automation attempt and its outcome. Unblocking this would require a human to manually clear the DataDome challenge (or solve it) in their own browser session, or a different (non-CAPTCHA-triggering) data source for the counts; status stays partial.
